(a) Study.—The Secretary shall conduct a study of the application of radiation to petroleum at standard temperature and pressure to refine petroleum products, whose objective shall be to increase the economic yield from each barrel of oil.  
    (b) Goals.—The goals of the study shall include—
        (1) increasing the value of our current oil supply;  
        (2) reducing the capital investment cost for cracking oil;  
        (3) reducing the operating energy cost for cracking oil; and  
        (4) reducing sulfur content using an environmentally responsible method.   
    (c) Authorization of Appropriations.—There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $250,000 for fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary to conduct a technical study and authorizes appropriations for it. One might assume a study implies outside expert input, but the text names no outside party, advisory body, comment period, hearing, rulemaking, or right to sue. Every actor is inside the federal government, and a study is not a decision made with outside consultation.
fable.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study of the application of radiation to petroleum at standard temperature and pressure to refine petroleum products

opus.w: The section only tells the Secretary to conduct a research study, lists the study's goals and authorizes funding. No one outside the federal government is consulted, joins an advisory panel or comments on a federal decision. A study's research topic, such as the oil industry, does not make it participation.
opus.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study of the application of radiation to petroleum at standard temperature and pressure to refine petroleum products
opus.b:
**Step 1. Reasoning:** One could be tempted to read the energy-research context as bringing in industry or outside scientists. It doesn't. The section only tells the Secretary to conduct a study and authorizes $250,000 for it. It names no outside party, no consultation, no comment period, no advisory body and no right to sue. Even if outside experts were used, Example 3 shows that consulting on the contents of a study is not participation in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to conduct an internal study. It does not mandate consultation with non-federal entities, public hearings, or advisory committees with outside members. The actors involved are solely within the federal government (the Secretary).
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study of the application of radiation to petroleum at standard temperature and pressure to refine petroleum products, whose objective shall be to increase the economic yield from each barrel of oil.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that a "study" implies gathering input from outside experts or stakeholders, thus constituting participation. However, the text only mandates that the Secretary *conduct* the study; it does not explicitly require consultation with non-federal entities, public comment, or an advisory board with outside members. The study is an internal agency action.
